question: In these Guidelines, the abbreviation PHA stands for:
explanation: Section 1.1 defines PHA as the Public Health Act (p.4).

question: In these Guidelines, the abbreviation CWA stands for:
explanation: Section 1.1 defines CWA as the Clean Water Act (p.4).

question: In these Guidelines, the letter K refers to:
explanation: Section 1.1 defines K as soil permeability or hydraulic conductivity (p.4).

question: In these Guidelines, the abbreviation lpd means:
explanation: Section 1.1 defines lpd as litres per day, a flow measure (p.4).

question: According to the conversion factors, 1 inch equals:
explanation: Section 1.2 states 1 in = 2.540 cm (p.5).

question: According to the conversion factors, 1 Imperial gallon (IG) equals:
explanation: Section 1.2 states 1 IG = 4.546 L (p.5).

question: According to the conversion factors, 1 US gallon (USG) equals:
explanation: Section 1.2 states 1 USG = 3.785 L (p.5).

question: According to the conversion factors, 1 acre equals:
explanation: Section 1.2 states 1 acre = 43,560 sq ft (p.5).

section: 1.3 Department of Public Safety (DPS), Technical Inspection Services Head Office
question: What is the mailing address of the DPS Technical Inspection Services Head Office?
options: 12 McGloin Street, 2nd Floor, Fredericton, NB E3A 5T8
10 King Street, 1st Floor, Fredericton, NB E3B 1E3
12 McGloin Street, 3rd Floor, Saint John, NB E2L 4S6
explanation: Section 1.3 gives the head office as 12 McGloin Street, 2nd Floor, Fredericton, NB E3A 5T8 (p.6).

section: 1.3 Department of Public Safety (DPS), Technical Inspection Services Head Office
question: What is the DPS toll free number listed in the Guidelines?
explanation: Section 1.3 lists the DPS toll free number as 1-844-249-6533 (p.6).

question: Under the Public Health Act, an on-site sewage disposal system is defined as:
options: Only a holding tank with an alarm
A septic tank with subsurface disposal field and all other systems not connected to an approved wastewater treatment facility
A pit privy with a vent
Any tank connected to a municipal sewer
explanation: Section 2 defines it as a septic tank with subsurface disposal field plus all other systems not connected to a wastewater treatment facility approved by the Minister under the CWA (p.6).

question: Who is required to be licensed and hold an approval?
options: Anyone installing, constructing, repairing, or replacing a system or any of its parts
explanation: Section 2 states it is mandatory that anyone installing, constructing, repairing, or replacing a system or any of its parts be licensed and have an approval (p.6).

question: Approvals are issued for wastewater from personal hygiene, sanitation, cooking and laundering. Which of the following is NOT covered?
explanation: Section 2 includes greywater but excludes liquid and water-carried wastes from industrial or manufacturing processes, sump pumps, gutters, drainage pipes and runoff water (p.6).

question: An engineered system is mandatory when the estimated daily sewage flow exceeds:
explanation: Section 2.1 requires engineered systems when estimated daily sewage flows exceed 5,460 L/d (p.7).

question: An engineered on-site sewage disposal system must be:
options: Designed by DPS staff and installed by anyone
Installed by a Licensee and designed by a Professional Engineer licensed through APEGNB
Designed by the Licensee and installed by the homeowner
Installed by a plumber with no design needed
explanation: Section 2.1 requires installation by a Licensee and design by a Professional Engineer licensed through the Association of Professional Engineers and Geoscientists of New Brunswick (p.7).

question: Which of these is a condition that makes an engineered system mandatory?
options: The system uses a plastic chamber
The lot is larger than one acre
Suitable imported sand is not available
explanation: Section 2.1 lists conditions including flows over 5,460 L/d, unsuitable soils, unavailable suitable imported sand, and effluent stronger than typical domestic wastewater (p.7).

question: What is the purpose of the soil in an on-site sewage disposal system?
options: To provide infiltration, dispersal, and final treatment of effluent before it reaches bedrock, groundwater or setbacks
To prevent freezing of the pipes
To support the weight of the tank
explanation: Section 3.1 states the soil provides infiltration, dispersal, and final treatment of effluent before it reaches bedrock, groundwater or horizontal setbacks (p.7).

question: Test holes must be located within what distance of the proposed disposal field?
explanation: Section 3.1 requires test holes within approximately 3 m (10 feet) of the proposed disposal field (p.7).

question: How deep must a test hole be?
options: At least 1.8 m (6 ft) unless bedrock is encountered
explanation: Section 3.1 requires the test hole to be at least 1.8 m (6 feet) deep unless bedrock is encountered (p.7).

question: Why should a test hole NOT be dug directly in the existing field area?
options: It makes the soil too compact
explanation: Section 3.1 warns that digging a test hole directly in the existing field area could contaminate groundwater (p.7).

question: An in-ground trench is permitted to be installed in which soil categories?
explanation: Section 3.1 states an in-ground trench is permitted in A, B or C soil (p.8).

question: Category D soil means the soil is too permeable or impermeable. What is required in that case?
options: A raised mound field or engineered design
explanation: Section 3.1 states Category D cannot be used to select a system, so a raised mound field or engineered design is required (p.8).

question: What is the Kfs range for Type A soil?
explanation: Section 3.1 gives Type A as 1x10-4 m/sec to 6x10-4 m/sec (p.8).

question: What is the Kfs range for Type C soil?
explanation: Section 3.1 gives Type C as 3x10-6 m/sec to 2x10-5 m/sec (p.8).

question: A moist soil sample forms a weak ball that only stays together if handled carefully, with flakes or very short ribbons 1.5 to 2.5 cm long, and feels grainy and not sticky. This indicates:
explanation: Table 6 describes Category C (Fair) sandy loam this way: weak ball, flakes or very short ribbons 1.5 to 2.5 cm, grainy and not sticky (p.42).

question: What is the purpose of an interceptor drain or diversion ditch?
options: To carry effluent to the field
To connect the tank to the house
To divert or intercept surface water and groundwater upslope of a disposal field
explanation: Section 3.2 states an interceptor drain or diversion ditch diverts or intercepts surface water and groundwater upslope of a disposal field to prevent saturation during wet seasons (p.9).

question: Where is an interceptor drain placed relative to the disposal field?
explanation: Section 3.2 places the interceptor drain upslope of the disposal field to stop water moving down the slope from saturating the field (p.9).

question: What is the required separation distance from a drilled well to the disposal field?
explanation: Table 1 in Section 3.3 requires 23 m (75 ft) from a drilled well to the disposal field (p.10).

question: What is the required separation distance from a drilled well to the septic tank?
explanation: Table 1 in Section 3.3 requires 15 m (50 ft) from a drilled well to the septic tank (p.10).

question: What separation distance applies to a dug well or sandpoint well from both the septic tank and the disposal field?
explanation: Table 1 in Section 3.3 requires 30 m (100 ft) from a dug well or sandpoint well to both the tank and the field (p.10).

question: What is the required separation from a body of water (normal high water mark, not used as a potable supply) to the disposal field?
explanation: Table 1 in Section 3.3 requires 15 m (50 ft); note that work within 30 m (100 ft) of a watercourse needs a Watercourse Alteration Permit (p.10).

question: For a body of water used as a designated potable water supply, what is the required distance from the septic tank?
explanation: Table 1 in Section 3.3 requires 90 m (300 ft) from the septic tank to a body of water used as a designated potable water supply (p.10).

question: What is the required separation distance from a building foundation to the disposal field?
explanation: Table 1 in Section 3.3 requires 3.0 m (10 ft) from a building foundation to the disposal field (1.5 m to the tank) (p.10).

question: What is the required separation distance from a property line or intermittent ditch to the disposal field?
explanation: Table 1 in Section 3.3 requires 3.0 m (10 ft) from a property line or intermittent ditch (p.10).

question: What is the required vertical separation from the invert (bottom) of the distribution pipe to limiting factors such as bedrock or groundwater?
explanation: Table 1 in Section 3.3 requires 1.2 m (4 ft) vertically from the pipe invert to limiting factors (p.10).

question: If work is to be done within 30 m (100 ft) of a wetland or watercourse, whose responsibility is it to contact the Department of Environment and Local Government and obtain permits?
explanation: Section 3.3.1 states it is the property owner's responsibility to ensure DELG is contacted and all necessary permits obtained (p.11).

question: Under the Clean Water Act, a wetland is land that has a water table at, near or above the surface and:
options: Sustains aquatic processes as shown by hydric soils, hydrophytic vegetation and wet-adapted biology
explanation: Section 3.3.1 defines a wetland as land with a water table at, near or above the surface that sustains aquatic processes indicated by hydric soils, hydrophytic vegetation and adapted biological activity (p.11).

question: An abandoned well exists within the setback distances of a proposed system. What must happen before an Approval is issued?
options: The system must be moved 100 m away
The well must be properly decommissioned or proof of decommissioning provided
The owner must fill it with sand only
explanation: Section 3.3.2 requires the well to be properly decommissioned or sufficient proof provided, with proof submitted along with the Notice of Installation (p.11).

question: For a vacant lot smaller than 4000 m2 (1 acre) approved by the Planning Commission prior to 1976, the Department may grant an exemption up to what maximum flow?
explanation: Section 3.3.3 allows an exemption up to a maximum of 1365 L/day EDSF for such lots, provided all separation distances are met (p.12).

question: Where should the well be located relative to the on-site sewage disposal system where possible?
explanation: Section 3.4 states the well should be located upslope of the on-site sewage disposal system where possible (p.13).

question: When assessing a lot, separation distances must be checked to bodies of water within what distance of any part of the proposed system?
explanation: Section 3.4 lists separation distances to bodies of water within 100 m (330 ft) of any part of the proposed system (p.13).

question: Estimated daily sewage flows must be calculated based on:
options: The size of the lot only
The number of bathrooms divided by two
The design flow criteria in Appendix D
explanation: Section 4.1 requires flows to be calculated based on the design flow criteria in Appendix D (p.14).

question: The disposal field must be sized based on the soil with the slowest permeability within what depth below the distribution pipe?
explanation: Section 4.2 requires sizing based on the slowest permeability within 1.2 m (4 feet) below the distribution pipe (p.14).

question: How does disposal field size change with flow and soil permeability?
options: It increases as flow increases and permeability decreases
It depends only on lot size
explanation: Section 4.2 states the disposal field size increases as the flow increases and soil permeability decreases (p.14).

question: What is the minimum liquid capacity of a prefabricated septic tank?
explanation: Section 4.3 requires a minimum liquid capacity of 3410 L (p.14).

question: A septic tank must have two compartments. What share of the total capacity must the first compartment hold?
explanation: Section 4.3 requires two compartments with the first equal to two-thirds of total septic tank capacity (p.14).

question: Why must a septic tank have baffles at the inlet and outlet ends?
options: To prevent short-circuiting or direct flow-through of effluent
explanation: Section 4.3 requires baffles at inlet and outlet to prevent short-circuiting or direct flow through of effluent (p.15).

question: Which tank material is NOT permitted?
explanation: Section 4.3 permits concrete, fibreglass or polyethylene; steel tanks are not permitted due to higher corrosion rates (p.15).

question: Prefabricated septic tanks must conform to which standard and show what?
options: CSA Standard B66 with a visible stamp
NSF Standard 46 with a date code
CSA Standard B65 with a serial plate
explanation: Section 4.3 requires prefabricated tanks to conform to the most recent CSA Standard B66 and have a visible stamp (p.14).

question: The septic tank effluent filter must meet which standard?
explanation: Section 4.3 requires an effluent filter meeting NSF Standard 46, easily accessible for maintenance (p.15).

question: What is the minimum slope of the pipe from the house to the septic tank?
options: 3 mm per 300 mm of length or 1%
explanation: Section 4.3 requires a minimum slope of 3 mm per 300 mm of length or 1% (p.15).

question: What is the minimum liquid depth in a septic tank?
explanation: Section 4.3 states the minimum liquid depth in a tank is 0.9 m (3 ft) (p.15).

question: Under Regulation 2009-137, a conventional system is a septic tank with subsurface disposal field with flows not exceeding:
explanation: Section 4.4 defines a conventional system as having sewage flows not exceeding 5460 lpd (p.17).

question: How must distribution lines be laid in a disposal field?
options: Parallel to the contour and perpendicular to groundwater flow
Down the slope of the land
explanation: Section 4.4 requires distribution lines laid parallel to the contour (across the natural slope) and perpendicular to groundwater flow (p.17).

question: A distribution box must be installed level and must have:
options: A baffle in front of the inlet
explanation: Section 4.4 requires a distribution box to be installed level with a baffle in front of the inlet (p.17).

question: What size of crushed rock should geotextile be placed over before backfilling?
explanation: Section 4.4 recommends geotextile over crushed rock (10 mm to 50 mm) before backfilling (p.17).

question: What is the minimum trench width for a pipe and stone system?
explanation: Table 2 in Section 4.4.1 gives a minimum trench width of 450 mm (18 in) (p.19).

question: What is the maximum trench length for a pipe and stone system?
explanation: Table 2 in Section 4.4.1 gives a maximum trench length of 15 m (50 ft) (p.19).

question: What depth of clean crushed stone is required under and over the distribution pipe?
explanation: Table 2 in Section 4.4.1 requires 200 mm under and 50 mm over the pipe (8 in / 2 in) (p.19).

question: What is the required slope of the perforated distribution pipe?
options: 50 mm per 15 m (2 in per 50 ft)
explanation: Table 2 in Section 4.4.1 requires a slope of 50 mm per 15 m (2 in per 50 ft) (p.19).

question: What is the minimum total field length for a pipe and stone disposal field?
explanation: Table 2 in Section 4.4.1 requires a minimum total field length of 60 m (200 ft) (p.19).

question: What are the soil cover requirements for a disposal field?
options: Minimum 10 cm cover with no topsoil needed
Minimum 30 cm cover with at least 10 cm of topsoil; cover not to exceed 60 cm
explanation: Section 4.4.1 requires a minimum 30 cm (12 in) of air-permeable soil cover with at least 10 cm (4 in) of topsoil, not exceeding 60 cm (24 in) unless alternative aeration is provided (p.19).

question: A raised mound system is needed when a test pit identifies:
options: A lot larger than one acre
Limiting factors such as bedrock, groundwater, impermeable soil, or soil that is too permeable
explanation: Section 4.4.2 lists limiting factors: bedrock, groundwater or seasonal high water table, impermeable soil like clay, or soil that is too permeable (p.21).

question: How must the area under a proposed mound be prepared?
options: Scarified parallel to the slope, with no equipment driven over the scarified area
explanation: Section 4.4.2 requires scarification parallel to the slope using a cultivator, mould board or chisel plough, with no equipment driven over the scarified area (p.21).

question: Imported sand for a mound must be placed in lifts not exceeding:
explanation: Section 4.4.2 requires sand placed in lifts not exceeding 300 mm so it does not settle after placement (p.21).

question: Before imported sand is placed for a mound, what must be done to the site?
options: Stumps removed and sod and root layers stripped
explanation: Section 4.4.2 requires stumps to be removed and sod and root layers stripped before imported sand is placed (p.21).

question: For imported sand, the material passing the 75 micrometre (No. 200) sieve must be:
options: 8% or less passing, with less than 5% recommended
explanation: Table 3 requires 8% or less passing the No. 200 sieve in the sand fraction, with less than 5% recommended (p.22).

question: What are the Table 3 specifications for D10 and Cu of imported sand?
explanation: Table 3 specifies D10 of 0.15 to 0.50 mm and Cu (D60/D10) of 1 to 6.0 in the sand fraction (p.22).

question: What is the required KFS (permeability) range for imported sand?
explanation: Table 3 specifies KFS of 5x10-5 to 6x10-4 m/s for imported sand (p.22).

question: When permeability is determined by laboratory hydraulic conductivity testing (Ks), what is the relationship to KFS?
options: KFS is typically Ks divided by 2
explanation: Section 4.4.2.1 notes that laboratory testing determines Ks, and KFS is typically Ks/2 (p.23).

question: In a mound disposal field, how wide must the apron be?
options: 6 m (20 ft) on all downslope ends and 3 m (10 ft) on all other sides
explanation: Section 4.4.2.2 requires the apron to be 6 m (20 feet) on all downslope ends and 3 m (10 feet) on all other sides (p.23).

question: What slope ratio is required for the taper of a mound disposal field?
explanation: Section 4.4.2.2 requires the taper at a 4:1 (horizontal:vertical) ratio from the edge of the apron to original ground elevation (p.23).

question: What is the required finished elevation of backfill above the top of the pipe in a mound?
options: 0.3 m to 0.6 m (1 ft to 2 ft)
explanation: Section 4.4.2.2 defines finished elevation as 0.3 m (1 ft) to 0.6 m (2 ft) of backfill above the top of the pipe, with at least 100 mm of topsoil finished with sod or seed (p.24).

question: What size of concrete leaching chamber is approved for use in New Brunswick?
options: 2.0 m x 2.0 m x 1.0 m deep
1.2 m x 2.4 m x 0.6 m deep
0.6 m x 1.2 m x 0.6 m deep
1.0 m x 2.0 m x 0.5 m deep
explanation: Section 4.4.3 states the approved size is 1.2 m x 2.4 m x 0.6 m deep (p.25).

question: How much coarse gravel is required around the outside of concrete leaching chambers, and what size is it?
options: Minimum 30 cm (12 in) of 19 mm to 76 mm (3/4 in to 3 in) gravel
explanation: Section 4.4.3 requires a minimum of 30 cm (12 in) of coarse gravel, classified as 19 mm to 76 mm (p.24).

question: Where more than one row of leaching chambers is required, what is the minimum centre-to-centre spacing?
explanation: Section 4.4.3 requires rows to be placed at a minimum of 6 m (20 ft) centre to centre (p.25).

question: For concrete leaching chambers, the distance to limiting factors is measured from where, and what is the minimum?
options: From the top of the unit, 0.6 m
From the bottom of the unit, at least 1 m (3.3 ft)
explanation: Section 4.4.3 requires the distance measured from the bottom of the unit (not the pipe invert), at least 1 m (3.3 ft) from limiting factors (p.25).

question: What is the maximum length of any one plastic infiltrative chamber distribution line?
explanation: Section 4.4.4 states no one line shall exceed 15 m (50 ft) (p.26).

question: For plastic infiltrative chambers, what is the minimum distance from the bottom of the trench (or unit) to a limiting factor?
explanation: Section 4.4.4 requires at least 1.0 m (3.3 ft) measured from the bottom of the trench or unit (p.27).

question: What sand must be used with plastic infiltrative chambers?
explanation: Section 4.4.4 requires sand meeting the manufacturer's specifications, with a soil analysis recommended if uncertain (p.26).

section: 4.4.4.1 Approved For Use in New Brunswick
question: Which of the following infiltrative chambers is approved for use in New Brunswick?
options: Quick4 Standard (4 ft) by Infiltrator Water Technologies
explanation: Section 4.4.4.1 lists Infiltrator Water Technologies products including Quick4 Standard (4 ft) as approved (p.27).

section: 4.4.4.1 Approved For Use in New Brunswick
question: Approved infiltrative chambers receive what reduction in total length compared to a perforated pipe and stone system?
explanation: Section 4.4.4.1 states each listed chamber receives a 50% reduction in total length required for a perforated pipe and stone system (p.28).

question: What is the minimum size of a holding tank?
explanation: Section 4.4.5 requires holding tanks to be sized for the estimated daily volume with a minimum of 9000 L (2000 IG) (p.28).

question: A holding tank must have a signalling device that activates when the tank is 80% full. If used with a pump, what additional interlock is required?
options: A warning device inter-wired with the pump to prevent pump operation when the tank is 90% full
explanation: Section 4.4.5 requires the alarm at 80% full, and with a pump the warning device must be inter-wired to prevent pump operation at 90% full (p.29).

question: Holding tanks are considered for temporary use such as special events or construction camps not exceeding:
explanation: Section 4.4.5 allows temporary use for special events or construction/work camps not exceeding 12 months; seasonal cottage use is not considered temporary (p.28).

question: Holding tanks must conform to which standard?
options: CSA Standard B-66 or certification of equivalency
explanation: Section 4.4.5 requires conformity to the most recent CSA Standard B-66 or certification of equivalency acceptable to the Minister (p.28).

question: What separation distances apply to a holding tank?
options: The same as those for septic tanks in Table 1
explanation: Section 4.4.5 states separation distances are the same as those for septic tanks in Table 1 (p.28).

question: What separation distances apply to a pit privy?
options: The same as for septic tanks in Table 1
explanation: Section 4.4.6 states the same separation distances apply as indicated for septic tanks in Table 1 (p.29).

question: An earthen pit or vault privy will only be considered when:
options: The lot has no greywater being discharged (no well, no electricity)
The lot is larger than one acre
explanation: Section 4.4.6 allows an earthen pit or vault privy only when the lot has no greywater discharge, i.e. no well and no electricity (p.29).

question: Child protection bars on a privy holding tank must be spaced so that:
options: A spherical object with a diameter of 100 mm (4 in) cannot pass
explanation: Section 4.4.6 requires bars spaced so a 100 mm (4 in) diameter sphere cannot pass, where public access is expected (p.29).

question: What are the depth limits for an earthen pit privy?
options: No more than 3 m deep with no separation needed
No more than 1.2 m (4 ft) below original grade, with minimum 1.2 m (4 ft) separation to limiting factors
explanation: Section 4.4.6 requires minimum 1.2 m (4 ft) separation to limiting factors and a pit depth not greater than 1.2 m (4 ft) below original grade (p.30).

question: A pump or siphon is required when the total linear length of the disposal field exceeds:
options: 150 m (500 ft) for pipe and stone, or 75 m (246 ft) for plastic infiltrators
explanation: Section 4.4.7 requires a pump/siphon when the field exceeds 150 m (500 ft) of pipe and stone or 75 m (246 ft) of plastic infiltrators (p.31).

question: If a pump is needed only because of elevation, the field is not considered pressure-dosed. If needed because of field size, the field must be pressure-dosed and the pump must dose at:
explanation: Section 4.4.7 requires pressure-dosed fields to be dosed at 50 to 75% of total capacity at any one time (p.32).

question: Before covering a pump chamber assembly, the Licensee must:
options: Contact DPS for inspection of the electrical components
explanation: Section 4.4.7 requires the Licensee to contact DPS for inspection of electrical components prior to covering the pump chamber assembly (p.32).

question: Which statement about pump chamber wiring is correct?
options: Wiring does not need to meet electrical codes
A receptacle may be installed inside the sump
There shall be no receptacle or junction box inside the sump, and all feeders shall be installed by a licensed electrical contractor
explanation: Section 4.4.7 prohibits receptacles or junction boxes inside the sump and requires feeders installed by a licensed electrical contractor (p.32).

question: A plastic infiltrative chamber disposal field where pressure-dosing is required is:
options: Not a conventional design and cannot be designed by a Licensee
explanation: Section 4.4.7 states such a field is not a conventional design and cannot be designed by a Licensee; it is a non-conventional design (p.32).

question: Grease chambers are typically required for:
options: Some commercial and institutional uses such as restaurants or school cafeterias
explanation: Section 4.4.8 states grease chambers are not usually required on residential lines but are required in some commercial and institutional applications such as restaurants or school cafeterias (p.34).

question: Why must chemical compounds that dissolve grease NOT be added to grease traps?
options: They clean out the trap, letting dissolved grease re-solidify in the disposal field, which may cause system failure
They make the trap too cold
explanation: Section 4.4.8 prohibits grease-dissolving chemicals because they let dissolved grease re-solidify in the disposal field and may cause the system to fail (p.35).

question: Effluent from an oil/water separator:
options: Is not permitted to be discharged to a domestic on-site sewage disposal system
May go to any domestic system
Can go to a pit privy
explanation: Section 4.4.9 prohibits discharge of oil/water separator effluent to a domestic on-site sewage disposal system (p.35).

question: Small amounts of chemicals such as paints, solvents or thinners in separator effluent are a concern because they:
options: Can kill the bacteria that break down organic matter in the system
explanation: Section 4.4.9 notes such chemicals can kill the bacteria that break down organic matter in an on-site sewage disposal system (p.36).

question: Under Section 24 of the Public Health Act, which of the following requires an approval?
options: Relocating a septic tank horizontally or vertically
explanation: Section 4.5 states an approval is required to install, construct, repair or replace a system, including relocating a septic or holding tank (p.36).

question: Which activity is listed as a repair requiring an application for approval?
options: Anytime an excavation is required within the limits of the disposal field, including the apron or taper
explanation: Section 4.5 lists excavation within the disposal field limits, including apron or taper, as a repair requiring approval (p.36).

question: If an investigation is needed to determine the scope of repairs, what must happen first?
options: Obtain an Approval first, with the application describing the planned investigative actions
explanation: Section 4.5 requires an Approval first when investigation is needed, with the application describing the investigative actions (p.36).

question: Under Regulation 09-137, a conventional system has sewage flows not exceeding 5460 litres per day. A non-conventional system is defined as:
options: Any system with a septic tank
An on-site sewage disposal system other than a conventional system
explanation: Section 4.6 defines a non-conventional system as an on-site sewage disposal system other than a conventional system (p.36).

question: Which of the following is an example of a non-conventional system?
explanation: Section 4.6 lists contour systems, sloping sand filters, package plants, pressure-dosed infiltrative chambers, peat filters, constructed wetlands and large diameter matted pipe as examples (p.36).

question: Installers licensed to install contour systems must follow which document?
options: The Selection and Installation Manual for Contour Sewage Disposal Systems in New Brunswick
explanation: Section 4.6 requires contour installers to follow the most recent Selection and Installation Manual for Contour Sewage Disposal Systems in New Brunswick (p.37).

question: How does someone apply for a non-conventional installer licence?
options: In writing to the Department of Public Safety with appropriate proof of training
explanation: Section 4.6 states a non-conventional licence can be applied for in writing to the Department of Public Safety with appropriate proof of training (p.37).

question: What is the licensing fee for a conventional installer licence?
explanation: Section 5.2 sets the conventional licensing fee at $400 (p.39).

question: What is the licensing fee for a non-conventional installer licence?
explanation: Section 5.2 sets the non-conventional licensing fee at $350 (p.39).

question: Installer licences are issued to:
explanation: Section 5.2.1 states licences are issued to a company/business, not to named individuals (p.40).

question: A conventional installer licence allows installation of mound, trench or area bed systems with pipe and stone, leaching chambers or infiltrative chambers, and includes holding tanks and pit privies, but excludes:
options: A contour system or an infiltrative chamber pressure-dosed system
explanation: Section 5.1 excludes a contour system and an infiltrative chamber pressure-dosed system from the conventional licence (p.39).

question: When do installer licences expire each year?
explanation: Section 5.2.1 states licences expire on March 31st of each year (p.40).

question: A licensed company must at all times employ at least one person who completed the course and passed the exam. If that person leaves, how long does the company have to appoint a replacement before the licence is revoked?
explanation: Section 5.2.1 allows 30 days from the employee's termination date to appoint a replacement, otherwise the licence is revoked (p.40).

question: In which month is the Provincial Installer Course offered each year?
explanation: Section 5.3 states the course is offered by Health Protection Services in April of each year (p.41).

question: To be eligible for the course, an applicant must pre-register with Health Protection Services at least:
options: Three weeks before the start of the month
explanation: Section 5.3 requires pre-registration at least three weeks before the start of the month (p.41).

question: What are the exam time limit and passing grade?
explanation: Section 5.3 grants a three-hour time limit with a passing grade of 85% (p.41).

question: During the exam, candidates are permitted to have:
options: The course slides and Technical Guidelines from the course handout package
explanation: Section 5.3 permits candidates to have the course slides and Technical Guidelines from the handout package during the exam (p.41).

question: A candidate who fails the exam twice must:
options: Take the course again before attempting the exam
explanation: Section 5.3 states those unsuccessful twice must take the course before again attempting the exam (p.41).

question: What is the application fee for an on-site sewage disposal system approval?
explanation: Section 5.4 sets the application fee at $150, received before assessment and non-refundable once processing starts (p.43).

question: Once a complete application is received, the Inspector will complete the application assessment within:
